docs.title: ICT operations manager
docs.text:
ICT operations managers coordinate ICT services and infrastructure ensuring that the organisation has the required infrastructural resources. They also plan and monitor stages of either a business process or a computer process, negotiate contracts and take mitigation action in case of non-fulfilment of agreements. They oversee the day-to-day tasks involving infrastructure components, ICT systems and software.
Also called: ICT data processing manager, data processing manager, ICT operations managers, IT data processing manager, IT process manager.
Essential skills: manage staff, track key performance indicators, innovation processes, define technology strategy, oversee quality control, use ICT ticketing system, develop ICT workflow, use different communication channels, manage budgets, design process, improve business processes, train employees.

docs.title: Software manager
docs.text:
Software managers oversee the acquisition and development of software systems in order to provide support to all organisational units. They also monitor the results and quality of the different software solutions and projects implemented in the organisation.
Also called: applications manager, software managers, ICT applications manager, software applications manager, soft manager.
Essential skills: manage ICT project, evaluate cost of software products, systems development life-cycle, execute analytical mathematical calculations, manage data, ICT project management methodologies, manage business knowledge, analyse software specifications, create software design, ICT project management, apply ICT system usage policies, organisational policies.

docs.title: Chief information officer
docs.text:
Chief information officers define and implement the ICT strategy and governance. They determine necessary resources for the ICT strategy implementation, anticipate ICT market evolutions and company business needs. They contribute to the development of the organisation's strategic plan and ensure that the ICT infrastructure supports the organisation's overall operations and priorities.
Also called: CIO, IT director, chief information officers.
Essential skills: software design methodologies, ensure adherence to organisational ICT standards, manage software releases, define technology strategy, implement corporate governance, software architecture models, maintain plan for continuity of operations, monitor technology trends, utilise decision support system, decision support systems, information structure, coordinate technological activities.

docs.title: ICT project manager
docs.text:
ICT project managers schedule, control and direct the resources, people, funding and facilities to achieve the objectives of ICT projects. They establish budgets and timelines, perform risk analysis and quality management, and complete project closure reports.
Also called: IT projects manager, IT project manager, web projects manager, web project manager, ICT project managers.
Essential skills: create project specifications, apply conflict management, internal risk management policy, estimate duration of work, recruit employees, perform project management, manage staff, quality standards, ICT project management methodologies, provide cost benefit analysis reports, perform risk analysis, manage budgets.

docs.title: ICT vendor relationship manager
docs.text:
ICT vendor relationship managers establish and maintain positive business relationships between stakeholders (external or internal), by deploying activities which are compliant with organisational processes. They also manage the outsourcing process for the organisation's ICT department and the supply chain communications.
Also called: ICT vendor relationships manager, ICT vendor relationship managers, IT vendor relationship manager, IT vendor relations manager, ICT vendor relations manager.
Essential skills: analyse supply chain strategies, maintain relationship with customers, manage budgets, manage contracts, coordinate purchasing activities, crowdsourcing strategy, contract law, ICT market, maintain relationship with suppliers, prepare purchasing reportings, outsourcing strategy, analyse supply chain trends.

docs.title: ICT product manager
docs.text:
ICT product managers analyse and define current and target status for ICT products, services or solutions. They estimate the cost effectiveness, points of risk, opportunities, strengths and weaknesses of products or services provided. ICT product managers create structured plans and establish time scales and milestones, ensuring optimisation of activities and resources.
Also called: IT product manager, IT products manager, ICT product managers, ICT products manager, ICT products managers.
Essential skills: assess ICT knowledge, ICT software specifications, perform market research, product comprehension, ICT market, define technical requirements, ICT hardware specifications, manage budgets, manage schedule of tasks, perform product planning, monitor technology trends, ICT infrastructure.

docs.title: Chief data officer
docs.text:
Chief data officers manage companies' enterprise-wide data administration and data mining functions. They ensure data are used as a strategic business asset at the executive level and implement and support a more collaborative and aligned information management infrastructure for the benefit of the organisation at large.
Also called: chief data officers, chief analytics officer, CDO.
Essential skills: information structure, visual presentation techniques, manage ICT data classification, data mining, decision support systems, manage ICT data architecture, apply information security policies, utilise decision support system, business processes, data storage, define data quality criteria, manage data.

docs.title: ICT information and knowledge manager
docs.text:
ICT information and knowledge managers contribute to the definition of organisational information strategy and apply information and knowledge creation, editing, storage, and distribution policies. They manage the maintenance and evolution of structured and unstructured information. They create digital structures to enable exploitation and optimisation of information and knowledge, manage data analysis and enable business intelligence.
Also called: ICT information manager, ICT knowledge manager, ICT information and knowledge managers, IT information and knowledge manager, IT information manager.
Essential skills: create data models, manage business knowledge, analyse the context of an organisation, assess informational needs, information security strategy, information extraction, data models, business processes, manage information sources, information architecture, unstructured data, decision support systems.

docs.title: ICT documentation manager
docs.text:
ICT documentation managers are in charge of managing the documentation development process in accordance with legal requirements, standards, organisational policies and goals. They schedule, control and direct the resources, people, funding and facilities of the documentation department (including establishing budgets and timelines, risk analysis and quality management). They also develop documentation standards, structuring methods and media concepts to effectively communicate product concepts and usage.
Also called: IT documentation manager, ICT documentation managers, documentation manager, technical communication manager.
Essential skills: ICT project management, manage budgets, manage content development projects, content development processes, industrial software, develop information standards, manage information sources, identify legal requirements, develop technological improvement strategies, perform resource planning, disseminate internal communications, ensure compliance with legal requirements.

docs.title: Telecommunications manager
docs.text:
Telecommunications managers coordinate telecommunications staff activities for installing, troubleshooting, repairing and maintaining telecommunications equipment and infrastructure. They oversee the research, evaluation and implementation of new technologies and ensure a safe working environment for the employees. They supervise the inventory of supplies as well as user and customer assistance actions.
Also called: telecom manager, telecommunications equipment manager, telecommunications managers, telecommunications installation manager, telecommunications development manager.
Essential skills: manage budgets, comply with legal regulations, recruit employees, coordinate technological activities, ICT communications protocols, manage staff, use ICT ticketing system, execute ICT audits, implement ICT risk management, service-oriented modelling.

docs.title: Chief technology officer
docs.text:
Chief technology officers contribute to a company's technical vision and lead all aspects of technology development, according to its strategic direction and growth objectives. They match technology with business needs.
Also called: chief technology officers, IT director, information technology director, CTO.
Essential skills: review development process of an organisation, utilise decision support system, manage budgets, optimise choice of ICT solution, maintain plan for continuity of operations, implement ICT coding conventions, ICT project management methodologies, administer ICT system, monitor ICT research, lead technology development of an organisation, ICT project management, define technology strategy.

docs.title: Gambling, betting, and lottery game developer
docs.text:
Gambling, betting, and lottery game developers create, develop and produce content for new lottery and similar games for large audiences.
Also called: gaming, betting, and lottery games developer, betting game designer and producer, game designer and producer, gambling, betting and lottery games designer and producer, betting, lottery and gambling games designer and producer.
Essential skills: Unity (digital game creation systems), digital game creation systems, id Tech, games rules, follow ethical code of conduct of gambling, use specialised design software, develop virtual game engine, player logic, adapt to changing situations, apply gaming psychology, CryEngine, Unreal Engine.

docs.title: Gambling, betting, and lottery quality assurance engineer
docs.text:
Gambling, betting and lottery quality assurance engineers design and plan methods to test the gambling, the lottery or betting games. They execute the tests. These games can be both for public or for private audience, and the tests are for both online and land-based gaming.
Also called: betting, gambling, and lottery quality controller, gambling, betting, and lottery quality controller, lottery, betting, and gaming quality assurance engineer, lottery, gaming, and betting quality assurance engineer, gaming, betting, and lottery quality assurance engineer.
Essential skills: follow ethical code of conduct of gambling, perform services in a flexible manner, probability theory, mathematics, attend gaming tests, solve problems in gambling through digital means, report gaming incidents, develop work plans to solve problems, legal standards in gambling.

docs.title: Actuarial consultant
docs.text:
Actuarial consultants analyse, manage and provide guidance on financial impact of risks. They can work in fields related to insurance, pension, investment, banking, healthcare etc. Actuarial consultants apply technical and statistical models and theories to give strategic, commercial, and financial advice.
Also called: actuary, consulting actuaries, actuarial advisor, insurance actuaries, actuarial mathematician.
Essential skills: financial products, obtain financial information, apply statistical analysis techniques, analyse market financial trends, create a financial plan, produce statistical financial records, actuarial science, perform risk analysis, synthesise financial information, statistics, advise on financial matters, provide support in financial calculation.

docs.title: Mathematician
docs.text:
Mathematicians study and deepen existing mathematical theories in order to expand the knowledge and find new paradigms within the field. They can apply this knowledge to challenges presented in engineering and scientific projects in order to assure that measurements, quantities, and mathematic laws prove their viability.
Also called: mathematics science researcher, mathematics research scientist, logic researcher, logic scholar, logic science researcher.
Essential skills: scientific modelling, think analytically, use logical reasoning, study the relationships between quantities, statistics, execute analytical mathematical calculations, apply scientific methods, scientific research methodology, conduct quantitative research, mathematics, create solutions to problems, algebra.

docs.title: Statistician
docs.text:
Statisticians collect, tabulate, and, most importantly, analyse quantitative information coming from a varied array of fields. They interpret and analyse statistical studies on fields such as health, demographics, finance, business, etc. and advise based on patterns and drawn analysis.
Also called: statistics researcher, statistics research analyst, statistic research associate, statistical data analyst, statistical scholar.
Essential skills: statistics, statistical analysis system software, apply scientific methods, identify statistical patterns, perform data analysis, execute analytical mathematical calculations, think analytically, conduct quantitative research, mathematics, data quality assessment, process data, scientific research methodology.

docs.title: Biometrician
docs.text:
Biometricians perform research in the field of biometrics. They carry statistical or biological research projects by measuring fingerprints, retinas, and human shapes for medical or industrial applications.
Also called: biometrics science researcher, biometrics analyst, biometric studies researcher, biometricians, biometric studies scholar.
Essential skills: plan research process, scientific research methodology, execute analytical mathematical calculations, interpret current data, scientific modelling, statistics, perform scientific research, biometrics, apply statistical analysis techniques, develop scientific research protocols, mathematics.

docs.title: Demographer
docs.text:
Demographers study a variety of parameters related with population. They develop, based on their observations, statistical analyses on the evolutions and changes of births, elderly, marriage and divorce, employment, mortality, immigration and related matters.
Also called: demography science researcher, demography scientist, demography research scientist, field demographer, demography studies scholar.
Essential skills: apply statistical analysis techniques, use a computer, use data processing techniques, statistics, forecast human population trends, study human population, execute analytical mathematical calculations, scientific research methodology, demography, perform scientific research, mathematics, apply scientific methods.

docs.title: Financial analyst
docs.text:
Financial analysts conduct economic research and elicit valuable analyses on financial matters such as profitability, liquidity, solvency, and asset management. They provide recommendations on financial matters for decision-making processes. Financial analysts work in both the public and the private sector.
Also called: financial markets report writer, structured finance analyst, financial markets analyst, company analyst, financial markets forecaster.
Essential skills: business processes, perform business analysis, accounting, statistics, interpret financial statements, advise on financial matters, microeconomics, prepare financial projections, perform business research, financial management, create a financial report, consider economic criteria in decision making.

docs.title: Financial risk analyst
docs.text:
Financial risk analysts correctly identify and review potential risk areas threatening the assets or capital of organisations. They specialise in either credit, market, operational or regulatory risk analysis. They use statistical analysis to evaluate risk, make recommendations to reduce and control risk and review documentation for legal compliance.
Also called: credit risk analysts, corporate risk department manager, consortia advisor, operational risk analyst, chief risk officer.
Essential skills: assessment of risks and threats, financial analysis, advise on risk management, risk transfer, economics, analyse financial risk, financial forecasting, financial management, manage financial risk, create risk maps, create risk reports, financial jurisdiction.

docs.title: Investment analyst
docs.text:
Investment analysts undertake research to make informed recommendations to fund managers. They research investments globally but depending on the nature and field of their employer they can specialise in fields like retail, infrastructure, energy, banking and financial services.  They focus on financial and economical information such as the political and economic developments that can impact financial markets, the financial performance of the target companies and use the interpretation of data from different sources to understand how it affects investment decision making.
Also called: investment compliance analyst, portfolio analyst, investment accounting analyst, investment banking analyst, investment specialist.
Essential skills: financial markets, analyse market financial trends, monitor stock market, financial products, provide support in financial calculation, actuarial science, obtain financial information, analyse economic trends, analyse financial performance of a company, stock market, international trade, funding methods.

docs.title: Mergers and acquisitions analyst
docs.text:
Mergers and acquisitions analysts oversee the execution of transactions for the purchase, sale, merger or takeover of companies. They negotiate and complete the deal on the client's behalf, by working closely with lawyers and accountants. Mergers and acquisitions analysts conduct operational and legal risk assessments of a company, assess comparable companies in the market and help with the post-merger integration.
Also called: mergers and acquisitions professional, acquisitions analyst, mergers analyst, M&A specialist, mergers and acquisitions banker.
Essential skills: make strategic business decisions, develop investment portfolio, modern portfolio theory, analyse market financial trends, analyse financial risk, analyse financial performance of a company, assess financial viability, manage contracts, provide support in financial calculation, analyse business plans, actuarial science, review investment portfolios.

docs.title: Securities analyst
docs.text:
Securities analysts perform research activities to gather and analyse financial, legal and economic information. They interpret data on the price, stability and future investment trends in a certain economic area and make recommendations and forecasts to business clients.
Also called: bonds analyst, securities research analyst, rating analyst, corporate securities research analyst, shares analyst.
Essential skills: review investment portfolios, collect financial data, obtain financial information, advise on investment, consult information sources, analyse financial risk, modern portfolio theory, financial products, actuarial science, financial markets, develop investment portfolio, analyse economic trends.

docs.title: Insurance rating analyst
docs.text:
Insurance rating analysts analyse information related to insurance markets and their credit rating, prepare rating reports and invoices, compile financial data and present and explain credit rating opinions to stakeholders, clients and external parties. They work for insurance companies and calculate the insurance premium and rates for the company’s clients using both manual and automated methods.
Also called: insurance analyst, insurance assessors, insurance assessor, insurance raters, insurance rater.
Essential skills: insurance market, types of insurance, analyse loans, credit control processes, actuarial science, advise on financial matters, principles of insurance, synthesise financial information, insurance law, prepare credit reports, obtain financial information, examine credit ratings.

docs.title: Middle office analyst
docs.text:
Middle office analysts work in the treasury of a financial company, ensuring compliance with company policy and legal legislation, providing research and analysis on financial matters, measuring risk and supporting operations in the front office.
Also called: middle office junior manager, senior analyst - control, middle office regulatory reform analyst, middle office specialist, middle office associate.
Essential skills: comply with legal regulations, conduct qualitative research, analyse financial risk, financial management, handle financial transactions, handle paperwork, office software, provide support in financial calculation, maintain records of financial transactions, banking activities, business processes, execute administration.

docs.title: Business intelligence manager
docs.text:
Business intelligence managers gain knowledge of the industry, the innovative processes therein, and contrast them with the operations of the company in order to improve them. They focus their analysis in the supply chain processes, warehouses, storage, and sales as to facilitate communication and revenue improvement.
Also called: business intelligence managers, business intelligence analyst, business intelligence consultant, business research analyst, competitive intelligence manager.
Essential skills: ensure compliance with policies, perform data analysis, perform business analysis, advise on efficiency improvements, manage business knowledge, statistics, analyse the context of an organisation, liaise with managers, statistical analysis system software, develop revenue generation strategies, business analysis, organisational policies.

docs.title: Business consultant
docs.text:
Business consultants analyse the position, structure and processes of businesses and companies and offer services or advice to improve them. They research and identify business processes such as financial inefficiencies or employee management and devise strategical plans to overcome these difficulties. They work in external consulting firms where they provide an objective view on a business and or company's structure and methodological processes.
Also called: business process consultant.
Essential skills: advise on financial matters, liaise with managers, analyse business plans, align efforts towards business development, identify undetected organisational needs, analyse business objectives, build business relationships, analyse the context of an organisation, business analysis, conduct qualitative research, conduct quantitative research, analyse external factors of companies.

docs.title: Business analyst
docs.text:
Business analysts research and understand the strategic position of businesses and companies in relation to their markets and their stakeholders. They analyse and present their views on how the company, from many perspectives, can improve its strategic position and internal corporate structure. They assess needs for change, communication methods, technology, IT tools, new standards and certifications.
Also called: standardisation expert, business strategy analyst, standardization expert, business development analyst, business strategy consultant.
Essential skills: conduct qualitative research, make strategic business decisions, analyse external factors of companies, market research, build business relationships, risk management, identify undetected organisational needs, analyse financial performance of a company, interpret financial statements, scientific research methodology, perform business analysis, analyse internal factors of companies.

docs.title: Manufacturing cost estimator
docs.text:
Manufacturing cost estimators collect and analyse data to evaluate the money, materials, labour and time required for manufacturing processes. They conduct analyses to identify (alternative) cost effective technical designs and production processes. They develop and use methods and tools for cost planning, controlling and analysis. They also perform quantitative and qualitative risk analyses and report on the development of costs.
Also called: manufacturing estimate clerk, estimator, production cost estimator, manufacturing cost analyst, manufacturing cost recovery technician.
Essential skills: execute analytical mathematical calculations, provide cost benefit analysis reports, mathematics, cost management, manufacturing processes, assess financial viability.

docs.title: ICT intelligent systems designer
docs.text:
ICT intelligent systems designers apply methods of artificial intelligence in engineering, robotics and computer science to design programs which simulate intelligence including thinking models, cognitive and knowledge-based systems, problem solving, and decision making. They also integrate structured knowledge into computer systems (ontologies, knowledge bases) in order to solve complex problems normally requiring a high level of human expertise or artificial intelligence methods.
Also called: AI system designer, linked data engineer, intelligent systems developer, semantic technologies engineer, designer of intelligent systems, machine learning systems designer.
Essential skills: systems theory, web programming, design application interfaces, manage database, design process, ICT security legislation, information structure, develop creative ideas, systems development life-cycle, database development tools, manage ICT semantic integration, business process modelling.

docs.title: Enterprise architect
docs.text:
Enterprise architects balance technological opportunities with business requirements. They also maintain a holistic view of the organisation's strategy, processes, information and ICT assets and link the business mission, strategy and processes to the ICT strategy.
Also called: enterprise developer, enterprise architects, enterprise architecture manager, enterprise designer.
Essential skills: design enterprise architecture, manage ICT data architecture, align software with system architectures, perform risk analysis, define software architecture, provide ICT consulting advice, execute feasibility study, information architecture, legal requirements of ICT products, object-oriented modelling, collect customer feedback on applications, keep up with the latest information systems solutions.

docs.title: ICT system developer
docs.text:
ICT system developers maintain, audit and improve organisational support systems. They use existing or new technologies to meet particular needs. They test both hardware and software system components, diagnose and resolve system faults.
Also called: ICT system developers, ICT systems developer, systems programmer, system developer, component developer.
Essential skills: use software libraries, migrate existing data, develop software prototype, integrated development environment software, interpret technical texts, ICT debugging tools, use software design patterns, analyse software specifications, tools for software configuration management, ICT system programming, computer programming, ICT system integration.

docs.title: ICT research consultant
docs.text:
ICT research consultants perform targeted ICT research and provide a final report to the client. They also use ICT tools to design questionnaires for surveys, analyse the results, write reports, present the results and make recommendations based on the research findings.
Also called: IT research consultant, ICT research specialist, ICT research advisor, ICT research consultants, IT research advisor.
Essential skills: execute ICT user research activities, interact with users to gather requirements, provide technical documentation, apply reverse engineering, conduct literature research, conduct research interview, develop software prototype, provide user documentation, utilise methodologies for user centered design, conduct quantitative research, innovate in ICT, create prototype of user experience solutions.

docs.title: Integration engineer
docs.text:
Integration engineers develop and implement solutions which coordinate applications across the enterprise or its units and departments. They evaluate existing components or systems to determine integration requirements and ensure that the final solutions meet organisational needs. They reuse components when possible and assist management in taking decisions. They perform ICT system integration troubleshooting.
Also called: software integration engineer, ICT integration engineers, IT integration engineer, system integration engineer.
Essential skills: ICT project management methodologies, integrate system components, provide technical documentation, apply company policies, procurement of ICT network equipment, apply ICT system usage policies, analyse network bandwidth requirements, use scripting programming, manage ICT system deployment, ICT system user requirements, ICT communications protocols, software components suppliers.

docs.title: Computer scientist
docs.text:
Computer scientists conduct research in computer and information science, directed toward greater knowledge and understanding of fundamental aspects of ICT phenomena. They write research reports and proposals. Computer scientists also invent and design new approaches to computing technology, find innovative uses for existing technology and studies and solve complex problems in computing.
Also called: ICT scientist, IT researcher, ICT science researcher, computers scientist, ICT research scientist.
Essential skills: scientific research methodology, write research proposals, synthesise research publications, conduct literature research, conduct quantitative research, apply statistical analysis techniques, apply reverse engineering, execute ICT user research activities, conduct scholarly research, conduct research interview, execute analytical mathematical calculations, conduct qualitative research.

docs.title: ICT business analyst
docs.text:
ICT business analysts are in charge of analysing and designing an organisation's processes and systems, assessing the business model and its integration with technology. They also identify change needs, assess the impact of the change, capture and document requirements and then ensure that these requirements are delivered whilst supporting the business through the implementation process.
Also called: ICT business analysts, business process specialist, IT business analyst.
Essential skills: identify customer requirements, legal requirements of ICT products, identify legal requirements, create business process models, analyse business processes, business requirements techniques, product usage risks analysis, interact with users to gather requirements, provide cost benefit analysis reports, analyse the context of an organisation, business process modelling, translate requirement concepts into visual design.

docs.title: ICT system architect
docs.text:
ICT system architects design architecture, components, modules, interfaces, and data for a multi-components system to meet specified requirements.
Also called: ICT systems architect, solution architect, IT systems architect, IT system architect, systems architect.
Essential skills: integrate system components, hardware platforms, design information system, analyse business requirements, web programming, apply ICT systems theory, systems theory, define technical requirements, use markup languages, database development tools, create data models, assess ICT knowledge.

docs.title: Embedded system designer
docs.text:
Embedded system designers translate and design requirements and the high-level plan or architecture of an embedded control system according to technical software specifications.
Also called: embedded software developer, embedded systems designers, embedded systems developer, embedded systems programmer, embedded system programmer.
Essential skills: engineering control theory, create software design, analyse software specifications, ICT communications protocols, interpret electronic design specifications, define technical requirements, provide ICT consulting advice, create flowchart diagram, systems development life-cycle, signal processing, real-time computing, develop creative ideas.

docs.title: Data analyst
docs.text:
Data analysts import, inspect, clean, transform, validate, model, or interpret collections of data with regard to the business goals of the company. They ensure that the data sources and repositories provide consistent and reliable data. Data analysts use different algorithms and IT tools as demanded by the situation and the current data. They might prepare reports in the form of visualisations such as graphs, charts, and dashboards.
Also called: data warehousing analyst, data analysts, data warehouse analyst, data storage analyst.
Essential skills: handle data samples, information categorisation, collect ICT data, interpret current data, data quality assessment, integrate ICT data, query languages, information structure, resource description framework query language, business intelligence, perform data mining, apply statistical analysis techniques.

docs.title: User experience analyst
docs.text:
User experience analysts assess client interaction and experience and analyse users' behaviours, attitudes, and emotions about the usage of a particular product, system or service. They make proposals for the improvement of the interface and usability of products, systems or services. In doing so, they take into consideration the practical, experiential, affective, meaningful and valuable aspects of human–computer interaction and product ownership, as well as the person's perceptions of system aspects such as utility, ease of use and efficiency, and user experience dynamics.
Also called: user experience officer, user experience analysts, usability analyst.
Essential skills: software interaction design, cognitive psychology, report analysis results, measure customer feedback, conduct qualitative research, conduct quantitative research, assess users' interaction with ICT applications, provide technical documentation, analyse business requirements, measure software usability, execute ICT user research activities, create prototype of user experience solutions.

docs.title: ICT system integration consultant
docs.text:
ICT system integration consultants advise on bringing together different systems to interoperate within an organisation for enabling data sharing and reducing redundancy.
Also called: systems integration consultant, system integration consultants, application integration consultant, network integration consultant, systems integration consultants.
Essential skills: integrate system components, systems development life-cycle, keep up with the latest information systems solutions, provide ICT consulting advice, apply information security policies, consult with business clients, monitor technology trends, attend to ICT systems quality, use scripting programming, define integration strategy, manage changes in ICT system, verify formal ICT specifications.

docs.title: ICT business analysis manager
docs.text:
ICT business analysis managers identify areas where information system changes are needed to support business plans and monitor the impact in terms of change management. They contribute to the general ICT functional requirements of the business organisation. ICT business analysis managers analyse business needs and translate them into ICT solutions.
Also called: ICT business analysis managers, IT business analysis director, IT business analysis manager, IT commercial analysis manager, ICT commercial analysis manager.
Essential skills: improve business processes, perform business analysis, ICT security legislation, define technical requirements, manage ICT project, provide cost benefit analysis reports, analyse business requirements, business processes, create business process models, write work-related reports, propose ICT solutions to business problems, design process.

docs.title: IT auditor
docs.text:
IT auditors perform audits of information systems, platforms, and operating procedures in accordance with established corporate standards for efficiency, accuracy and security. They evaluate ICT infrastructure in terms of risk to the organisation and establish controls to mitigate loss. They determine and recommend improvements in the current risk management controls and in the implementation of system changes or upgrades.
Also called: ICT auditor, IT Quality Appraiser, information technology auditor.
Essential skills: develop audit plan, audit techniques, quality standards, ICT security standards, improve business processes, prepare financial auditing reports, ICT security legislation, ICT process quality models, analyse ICT system, perform security vulnerability assessments, execute ICT audits, engineering processes.

docs.title: Data scientist
docs.text:
Data scientists find and interpret rich data sources, manage large amounts of data, merge data sources, ensure consistency of data-sets, and create visualisations to aid in understanding data. They build mathematical models using data, present and communicate data insights and findings to specialists and scientists in their team and if required, to a non-expert audience, and recommend ways to apply the data.
Also called: data scientists, data engineer, research data scientist, data expert, data research scientist.
Essential skills: manage data collection systems, online analytical processing, data models, implement data quality processes, information categorisation, visual presentation techniques, data mining, build recommender systems, report analysis results, statistics, handle data samples, normalise data.

docs.title: ICT system analyst
docs.text:
ICT system analysts specify the system needs to meet the end user requirements. They analyse system functions in order to define their goals or purposes and to discover operations and procedures for accomplishing them most efficiently. They also design new IT solutions to improve business efficiency and productivity, produce outline designs and estimate costs of new systems, specify the operations the system will perform, and the way data will be viewed by the end user. They present the design to the users and work closely with the users to implement the solution.
Also called: IT system analyst, IT systems analyst, network analyst, ICT systems analysts, ICT system analysts.
Essential skills: apply statistical analysis techniques, monitor system performance, analyse ICT system, design information system, create data models, ICT infrastructure, software architecture models, interact with users to gather requirements, systems development life-cycle, software metrics, identify customer requirements, analyse software specifications.

docs.title: ICT consultant
docs.text:
ICT consultants provide advice on how to optimise the use of existing tools and systems, make recommendations for the development and implementation of a business project or technological solution and contribute to project definitions. They raise awareness on information technology innovations and their potential value to a business. They also participate in the assessment and choice of ICT solutions.
Also called: ICT advisor, IT advisor, ICT ERP consultant, IT consultant, ICT consultants.
Essential skills: solve ICT system problems, monitor system performance, verify formal ICT specifications, ICT system integration, identify customer requirements, manage standard enterprise resource planning system, manage changes in ICT system, optimise choice of ICT solution, legal requirements of ICT products, analyse ICT system, keep up with the latest information systems solutions, visual presentation techniques.

docs.title: Green ICT consultant
docs.text:
Green ICT consultants advise organisations on their green ICT strategy and its implementation in the most effective and efficient manner to allow the organisation to reach their short, mid, and long term ICT environmental objectives.
Also called: green IT consultant, ICT sustainability systems consultant, IT environmental consultant, ICT environmental consultant, green ICT consultants.
Essential skills: define technical requirements, report on environmental issues, manage environmental impact of operations, ICT environmental policies, provide ICT consulting advice, create project specifications, promote environmental awareness, ensure compliance with environmental legislation, optimise choice of ICT solution, apply business acumen, consult with business clients.

docs.title: Software architect
docs.text:
Software architects create the technical design and the functional model of a software system, based on functional specifications. They also design the architecture of the system or different modules and components related to the business' or customer requirements, technical platform, computer language or development environment.
Also called: software architects, software designer, application architect.
Essential skills: object-oriented modelling, define software architecture, analyse business requirements, unified modelling language, create software design, provide technical documentation, provide cost benefit analysis reports, tools for software configuration management, analyse software specifications, create flowchart diagram, define technical requirements, collect customer feedback on applications.

docs.title: Software developer
docs.text:
Software developers implement or program all kinds of software systems based on specifications and designs by using programming languages, tools, and platforms.
Also called: application developer, application programmer, solutions developer, programmer, software specialist.
Essential skills: engineering principles, define technical requirements, use software design patterns, use software libraries, debug software, identify customer requirements, interpret technical requirements, provide technical documentation, develop software prototype, utilise computer-aided software engineering tools, analyse software specifications, integrated development environment software.

docs.title: User interface developer
docs.text:
User interface developers implement, code, document and maintain the interface of a software system by using front-end development technologies.
Also called: front end developer, UI programmer, user interface developers, UI developers, UI developer.
Essential skills: graphics editor software, use software design patterns, integrated development environment software, style sheet languages, analyse software specifications, utilise methodologies for user centered design, design user interface, software UI design patterns, design graphics, web programming, interpret technical texts, develop software prototype.

docs.title: Software analyst
docs.text:
Software analysts elicit and prioritise user requirements, produce and document software specifications, test their application, and review them during software development. They act as the interface between the software users and the software development team.
Also called: application analyst, programming analyst, programmer analyst, software analysts, software requirement analyst.
Essential skills: ICT system user requirements, create data models, develop software prototype, define software architecture, software design methodologies, interact with users to gather requirements, business requirements techniques, identify ICT user needs, define technical requirements, data models, manage ICT legacy implication, software architecture models.

docs.title: User interface designer
docs.text:
